story.head: Something has to change for the Canucks
paras: The Canucks are on a seven-game losing streak, and the Mammoth are winless in four (0-2-2). The Canucks played last night, and the Mammoth are rested. Going in, the Canucks are last in the NHL and the Mammoth fifth in the Central (tied for 14th in the NHL).

The Canucks haven’t played well, but their record (.167) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .335, and their goaltending has held them back. The Mammoth have played better than their record (.550) says: their chances are worth about .697, and their goaltending has held them back.
In their seven-game skid, the Canucks have been outscored 30-14, including 18-9 at 5-on-5.

The Canucks have had shaky goaltending (32nd), have a leaky penalty kill (32nd) and ice the puck a lot (31st). Vancouver has allowed 4.52 goals a game, the most in the league. On the other side, the Mammoth rarely get pinned in their own end (1st), let the point shots come and guard the net (1st) and roll their lines more evenly than almost anyone (3rd). The Mammoth are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Canucks. Beyond that, both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it.

Elias Pettersson (#40) (5 G / 16 A / 21 P in 21 GP) leads the Canucks in scoring, and Brock Boeser (7 G / 11 A / 18 P in 21 GP) has a team-high seven goals. For the Mammoth, Clayton Keller (5 G / 20 A / 25 P in 20 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games and a point in six straight games against Vancouver. Mikhail Sergachev (5 G / 15 A / 20 P in 20 GP) isn’t far behind.
Kevin Lankinen (1-8-0 / .805 SV% in 8 GS) has struggled for Vancouver so far, but will likely start. Karel Vejmelka (6-6-1 / .876 SV% in 13 GS) is in line to start for Utah.
The Mammoth usually control more of the chances than the Canucks do.

items.text: The Mammoth are newly without Nate Schmidt, Nick Schmaltz and Dylan Guenther, and have been without John Marino since Oct 17. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Avalanche are missing more right now.
The Canucks have been without Thatcher Demko all season. Kevin Lankinen is expected to start.
Brock Boeser has seven goals on chances worth about 3.7 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
